title: cassia brachiata
intro: Cassia brachiata, commonly known as Chakramardini in Ayurvedic medicine, is a small, deciduous shrub or tree native to India and Sri Lanka. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including the ability to reduce inflammation, manage diabetes, and exhibit antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Cassia brachiata include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective effects, which may contribute to its traditional use in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Cassia brachiata include flavonoids, alkaloids, and terpenoids, which are believed to be responsible for its medicinal properties.
